stem: A repeated out-of-range pH result is obtained with a verified meter and correct sample. What should happen next?
choices: Follow the controlled accept, hold, escalate, or authorized-adjustment procedure now that sample identity and meter performance have been verified; do not invent an unapproved chemistry change.
Repeat the measurement until two readings agree within the target range, because repeated testing is the best way to distinguish a transient outlier.
Replace the measured result with the recipe target in the batch record and investigate the instrument after production is complete.
Change more than one ingredient in small increments until pH enters range, then document the total adjustment as a single correction.
rationale: Once the sample and measurement system have been verified, the out-of-range pH should be treated as a real batch condition unless evidence shows otherwise. The next step is governed by the controlled batch procedure: accept, hold, escalate, or make only an explicitly authorized adjustment. Repeated testing cannot be used to shop for an in-range number, and ad hoc multi-ingredient corrections make both chemistry and traceability harder to interpret.
